---
description: window as the model is told it - what the tool does, and what each of its arguments is.
doing: going over what it holds
arguments:
  let_go: The things to let go of, each by its name as the list gives it, with a note of your own where you want one in its place - what you took from it. Each becomes one line that says what it was, its size and how to bring it back.
  bring_back: The things to bring back whole, each by its name.
  handoff: To go on in a fresh window - note, what you know and still mean to do; keep, the names of the things to keep whole. Everything else leaves the window, and can be brought back.
---
Lists what your window holds after your opening instructions and your tools, which always stay: each thing by its name, what it is, its size in tokens, its age (how many of your calls have gone since it came in), and whether it is carried or let go. With nothing asked, that list is the answer.

Names say what a thing is: prompt:<marker> for a slice of the prompt, lore:<id> for a lore entry, briefing:<section> for a section of the briefing, given:<name> for an item given by name, carry for what the session carries, call:<id> for the result of one of your calls, and work:<first call id>..<last call id> for a stretch of your own work, everything from the first call to the results of the last.

What you let go of, bring back or hand off changes your requests from your next call on, all of it in one step. The answer says what each later call is spared and what your next call costs once, as the provider's cache is written again from the first change on.
